title: Roman to Integer
statement: Convert a valid Roman numeral `s` to an integer. Subtractive pairs are IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, and CM.
constraints: s is a valid Roman numeral in the range 1..3999
hints: If a smaller value appears immediately before a larger value, subtract it instead of adding it.
Scanning right to left also works: add the symbol, and remember the previous value so a smaller symbol becomes negative.

approaches.name: Replace subtractive pairs, then sum
approaches.explanation: Turn IV into IIII-equivalent by subtracting.

approaches.name: One pass comparing neighbors
approaches.explanation: Add values[s[i]] with a sign chosen by the next symbol.

editorial: Walk left to right. If the current symbol is smaller than the next one, subtract its value. Otherwise add it. The last symbol is always added. This encodes every subtractive pair without a special-case table, and it rejects nothing because the problem promises a valid numeral.
